title: Deep Hierarchical Knowledge Loss for Fault Intensity Diagnosis

problem.claim: Fault intensity diagnosis is important in intelligent manufacturing.

gap.claim: Neglecting dependencies among target classes hinders practical deployment of fault intensity diagnosis.

contributions.claim: A general framework using deep hierarchical knowledge loss is introduced to support hierarchically consistent representation and prediction.
A hierarchical tree loss, focal hierarchical tree loss, and tree-height-based adaptive weighting schemes are developed to model hierarchical constraints and improve extensibility.
A group tree triplet loss with a hierarchical dynamic margin is proposed to model boundary structural knowledge across classes using hierarchical group concepts and tree distance.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the proposed framework and several loss components as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The joint losses significantly improve recognition of subtle faults.
Experiments on four real-world datasets from various industrial domains reportedly show superior results and outperform recent state-of-the-art fault intensity diagnosis methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fault intensity diagnosis matters in intelligent manufacturing, but ignoring dependencies among target classes limits deployment.
The paper introduces a deep hierarchical knowledge loss framework for hierarchically consistent representation and prediction.
Hierarchical tree losses and adaptive weighting schemes model class relationships and support extensibility.
A group tree triplet loss uses hierarchical groups, tree distance, and dynamic margins to model boundary structure.
The authors report improved subtle-fault recognition and superior results across four real-world industrial datasets.
